page: Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-amd is a virtual private server belonging to the High Performance family, configured with 1 shared vCPU and 2.0 GB of system memory. The underlying processor is an AMD EPYC x86_64 CPU operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. This single-core, single-thread allocation features a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Storage is provided via a local 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this server type.

Benchmark data reveals highly polarized performance characteristics. In single-core processing, the server achieves top-tier results, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 10% at 3314.98. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also perform strongly, with gzip compression reaching 30.88 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 13.91 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. However, due to the single shared vCPU configuration, multi-core performance is weak, ranking in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is generally constrained, with PassMark memory scores and read-only memory bandwidth tests falling into the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively, though large-block write bandwidth remains average at 28.69 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this instance lies in its shared CPU allocation and limited memory capacity, which restrict its utility for concurrent or memory-heavy workloads. PassMark database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput all rank in the bottom 10%, indicating that the server is not optimized for high-traffic database hosting or high-throughput web serving. Qualitatively, the server offers a budget-friendly entry point for lightweight, single-threaded tasks that benefit from modern AMD EPYC instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography. Appropriate workloads include basic utility scripting, lightweight single-threaded background workers, development environments, and low-demand microservices.
description: The Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-amd is an entry-level virtual server featuring 1 shared AMD EPYC vCPU, 2.0 GB of RAM, and 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor operates at 2.0 GHz with a 32 MB L3 cache. Benchmark results highlight strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance placing in the top 10% and single-threaded compression tasks ranking in the top 25%. However, the shared single-core configuration limits multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations, resulting in weak multi-core CPU performance and poor database and web-serving throughput. This server represents a cost-efficient option for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, such as basic utility scripts, development environments, and low-traffic microservices, where high multi-core concurrency and massive memory bandwidth are not required.
